answer: Sybil resistance can rest on one-time nullifiers, not identity checks. Each agent derives a marker from a credential only a distinct entity holds; the registry stores the spent set. Derivation is deterministic: a second enrolment reproduces the marker and is refused on collision, so cloning gains nothing. An attacker must rent separate entities from auditable, slashable issuers, so bought markers leave a trail that echoes back to the seller. A narrow ridge divides honest scale from farming: one crossing each, uniqueness proven, nothing else revealed; duplicates leave a hollow record.
